title: Project-hire trial and activation playbook
content:
Purpose:
This doc proposes a standardized project-based paid trial (PTP) for junior to mid-level IC roles in Eng/Product. Goal: shorten time-to-impact, evaluate in-context behavior (cross-team comms, code integration, product sense), provide a candidate experience that mirrors day-1 work.

High-level hypothesis:
- A short, structured paid project (5-10 days) yields stronger signal than take-home exercises and fewer false negatives when paired with a lightweight rubric and onboarding activation checklist.
- Success metric: reduce time-to-offer by 25% for targeted roles; increase first-90-day OKR attainment by improving expectation alignment.

Scope / When to use PTP:
- Use for IC1-IC3 software engineering roles, product analysts, and technical program roles where execution on a real ticket matters.
- Avoid for senior principal roles (use deep interviews) or strictly research roles.

Trial structure (recommended):
1) Pre-screen (30 min) — recruiter + hiring-manager quick fit (culture, availability, basic skills).
2) Paid project brief (2 business days to accept; candidate has 5 working days) — clear spec, 1-2 deliverables, small dataset or stub service, CI/unit test scaffold.
3) Live pairing demo (60 min) — candidate walks through approach, decisions; 1 live pairing session with engineer.
4) Debrief (30 min) — hiring manager + tech lead + recruiter alignment call.

Compensation model:
- Flat fee: $600-$1200 depending on level and scope (benchmarked to market freelance rates).
- Contract: contractor agreement + NDAs pre-signed by candidate.

Evaluation rubric (quick scorecard) — each axis 1-5 (1 low — 5 high). Weight in parentheses:
- Problem framing & clarity (20%) — did candidate clarify requirements, ask right questions, surface edge cases?
- Implementation correctness (25%) — tests pass, approach valid w.r.t constraints, no obvious correctness bugs.
- Code quality & maintainability (20%) — modularity, naming, small tests, PR description.
- Communication & collaboration (15%) — documents assumptions, responds to feedback, pair session clarity.
- Product/context judgment (10%) — tradeoffs, prioritization, safety/privacy awareness.
- Velocity & delivery (10%) — met deadline, shipped runnable artifact.

Decision matrix (example):
- Offer: weighted avg >= 4.0 AND no axis <= 3 unless hiring manager signs off.
- On hold / second sample: weighted avg 3.2-3.9 OR >1 axis = 2.
- Reject: weighted avg < 3.2 OR serious safety/ethical/privacy concerns.

Templates (to copy into GH PRs / recruiter messages):
- Project brief header: background, success criteria (explicit), input artifacts, constraints, acceptance checklist, submission format, deadline, compensation.
- Candidate feedback template: short bullets per rubric axis + recommended next step.

Onboarding activation checklist (for hires converted from trial) — first 10 days focused on velocity and context:
Pre-Day-1 (owned by People Ops / IT / Eng TPM):
- IT provisioning: laptop image request submitted (mac/linux), VPN, VPN profile, MDM, base tooling (editor, Docker, gh, AWS CLI) — noted as in-progress.
- Access: GitHub org invite, Jira project access, internal Confluence group, infra read-only keys, billing entries removed.
- Paperwork: contract scanned, payroll set up, expense card ordered.
- Buddy assigned: buddy = previous trial reviewer when possible.

Day 0-2:
- Welcome 30m: intro to team, org chart, product vision quick tour (PM + Eng lead).
- Local dev setup documented + smoke tests (run <30m).
- Small quick-win ticket assigned (clone of trial or similar) with pair mentor.
- 1:1 scheduling: manager meets thrice in first 14 days.

Day 3-10:
- Deep-dive onboarding sessions: infra, deployment flow, monitoring, SLOs, error budgets.
- Access review: ensure CI pipelines, secrets, service accounts are in place.
- 30-day onboarding goals set and shared in Confluence.

30/60/90 activation milestones (templates):
- 30d: own one small feature or bug from spec->deploy with mentor review.
- 60d: lead a cross-team micro-project, present impact metrics.
- 90d: independent contributor on primary team OKR, candidates for buddy mentoring.

Operational notes (open items / questions):
- Legal: need standardized contractor agreement appendix for paid trials (Salaried vs contractor implications). Legal contact: Maya Patel (cc).
- Payment flow: how to invoice? People Ops to discuss with finance for 1099/freelance process.
- Data sensitivity: for tickets touching PII, provide redacted dataset or sandbox environment.
- Candidate capacity: we need a small pool of reviewers willing to do quick pair sessions; propose rotating 1-2 engineers per week.

Signals to track (metrics):
- Trial acceptance rate (% of invited who accept brief).
- Trial-to-offer conversion rate.
- Offer acceptance rate.
- 90-day retention and time-to-first-merge for hires from PTP vs non-PTP.
- Hiring cycle time (requisition open -> offer).

Notes to self / async comments: 
- keep project briefs under 6 hours work for candidate -> respect time (candidates often have other interviews).
- try one round in Q1 2026 for 8 IC1 hires in core infra; measure conversion and first-90-day performance.
- coordinate with solutions-eng to create reproducible sandbox images for infra tickets.

Next steps (owners + rough ETA):
- Legal draft contractor appendix: Maya Patel — due 2025-12-05.
- Finance payment path (card vs invoice): Jordan Lee — due 2025-12-12.
- Pilot cohort: Eng hiring manager (Liam Chen) to run 8 trials — start 2026-01-08.
- Create 4 starter brief templates (web service, data ETL, small infra task, product bugfix) — People Ops + Eng SRE — due 2025-12-18.

Unresolved questions to review in pilot kickoff:
- How to treat internal referrals? (prefer pipeline vs trial bypass?)
- Standard compensation for non-US candidates (currency + tax).
- Which roles get waived from paid trial? (senior, urgent hires?)

Final thought: keep candidate experience front-and-center. A transparent brief + reasonable compensation communicates respect and improves brand. This is intended to be iterative — capture lessons and fold into hiring handbook on Confluence.
